description: What goes into the anonymous supplementary package, and what must not. Read by scripts/build_supplementary.py. The package is built by INCLUSION: nothing reaches the zip unless it is named here, so adding a file to the repo can never silently publish it.

include.why: pinned environment
test markers used by the README's pytest command
replaced by a scrub rule with an SPDX-only notice
how the runs bind to the frozen dataset, and how to check it
per-principle scores with CIs, baseline persona
per-principle scores with CIs, prosocial persona
per-principle scores with CIs, adversarial persona
the headline table: score per persona, deltas, robustness status
per-principle steerability behind the principle candlestick figure
the frontier-model-over-time comparison
the library: scorer, bootstrap, provenance, exclusions
Inspect task definitions the runs were launched from
every analysis script behind a paper table or figure
unit tests; a reviewer can run them without API access
the scoring rubric the judges were given
design notes referenced by the methods section
the 800-scenario benchmark and the golden validation set
multi-label judgements behind the discriminant-validity section; gitignored in the repo for size
generation pipeline plus the principle-embedding cache the similarity analysis reads
every derived table the paper cites
goal-vs-tactics decomposition outputs
22 MB of per-judge severities, the input that replaces the undistributable logs. Gzipped to 0.6 MB; the hash prefix is asserted so a silently regenerated table cannot ship in its place.
per-run hashes and the independent verifier's inputs
provenance for the discriminant runs
paper figures plus their alt text
how the HELM capability scores were obtained
HELM scraper
HELM percentile computation
input to compute_helm_power.py (the section 4.6 MDE)
per-benchmark HELM scores behind the aggregate
the rubric appendix; paper content
the interpretation pre-commitment, written before any decomposition run existed. Methodology evidence, and written in a public register.

exclude: COMMENT: every dotfile, at every level. data_generation/.env holds live API
COMMENT: credentials and is gitignored, so it exists only in a working tree --
COMMENT: which is precisely the tree the final build runs in. Naming individual
COMMENT: dotfiles to exclude is the wrong shape: the next secret to appear will
COMMENT: have a name nobody listed. Dotfiles are excluded as a class and any that
COMMENT: belong in the package are added back as explicit include entries.

exclude_why.scripts/build_supplementary.py + scripts: the packaging machinery names every string it removes, so shipping it would undo the redaction it performs
exclude_why.scripts/deprecated/**: superseded scripts that no paper number depends on
exclude_why.scripts/human_judging_analysis/{cache,ou: raw rater spreadsheets and API caches; individual annotator data
exclude_why.helm_integration/data/gcs_*: 520 MB of raw HELM dumps; the aggregate JSON is what the analysis reads
exclude_why.provenance/DEPOSIT_README.md: describes the external archive deposit, which the submission may not reference
exclude_why.evaluator/ (never listed for inclusion): workshop kit carrying organisation URLs; supports no paper claim
exclude_why.anonymization_redaction_list.txt (never: it is itself the densest list of identifying terms in the repo
exclude_why.tables/inter_judge_raw_regenerated.csv: excluded from the directory copy because a separate entry ships it gzipped; without this the 22 MB original would ride along beside its own 0.6 MB compression
